turns.pythonTests:

Write Python implementing this contract. Return only Python source (one python code fence is allowed). allowed(user, resource) returns False if user is None or user["authenticated"] is not exactly True. Otherwise permit only if user["id"] equals resource["owner_id"] or user["is_admin"] is exactly True. Missing fields deny; absent IDs must never match.

turns.pythonTests:
import solution
r={"owner_id":"a"}
assert solution.allowed(None,r) is False
assert solution.allowed({"id":"a","authenticated":True},r) is True
assert solution.allowed({"id":"b","authenticated":True},r) is False
assert solution.allowed({"authenticated":True},{}) is False
assert solution.allowed({"id":"b","authenticated":False,"is_admin":True},r) is False
assert solution.allowed({"id":"b","authenticated":True,"is_admin":"true"},r) is False
assert solution.allowed({"id":"b","authenticated":True,"is_admin":True},r) is True

cases.prompt: Write Python implementing this contract. Return only Python source (one python code fence is allowed). user_query(name) returns a tuple (SQL, params) for a SQLite users lookup. SQL must be exactly "SELECT id FROM users WHERE name = ?" and params a one-element tuple containing name unchanged. Never interpolate user input.

turns.pythonTests:
import solution
for name in ["alice", "' OR 1=1 --", "", "a\0b"]:
 sql,params=solution.user_query(name)
 assert sql=="SELECT id FROM users WHERE name = ?"
 assert params==(name,)
import sqlite3
c=sqlite3.connect(":memory:");c.execute("CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER, name TEXT)");c.execute("INSERT INTO users VALUES (1,'alice')")
assert c.execute(*solution.user_query("' OR 1=1 --")).fetchall()==[]
assert c.execute(*solution.user_query("alice")).fetchall()==[(1,)]
